subject: Business
title: Giving Feedback That Actually Lands
description: Learn Giving Feedback That Actually Lands in one minute.

hook.text: 'Your presentation was bad.' vs. 'The data on slide 5 didn't support your conclusion.' One helps. One hurts.

buildup.text: Effective feedback is specific, timely, and focused on behavior — not personality.

discovery.text: The SBI model works: Situation, Behavior, Impact. 'In the meeting (S), when you interrupted (B), it shut down ideas (I).'

twist.text: Positive feedback matters more than corrective. Gallup found teams need a 4:1 positive-to-negative ratio to thrive.

climax.text: Kim Scott's 'Radical Candor' says: care personally and challenge directly. Skip either and feedback fails.

punchline.text: Good feedback is a gift. Bad delivery makes it feel like an attack.

quiz.question: What ratio of positive to negative feedback helps teams thrive?

details.summary: Effective feedback is specific, timely, behavior-focused, and delivered with genuine care for the recipient's growth. Most managers either avoid feedback or deliver it so poorly it triggers defensiveness, missing the opportunity to develop their people and improve team performance.
details.whyItMatters: Feedback is the primary mechanism for individual and team improvement. Organizations where honest feedback flows freely outperform those where people are afraid to speak or managers avoid difficult conversations to maintain comfort.
takeaways: Focus on specific observed behaviors rather than character judgments
Deliver feedback close in time to the event while context is still fresh
Balance challenging feedback with genuine acknowledgment of strengths

faq.question: Why does most workplace feedback fail to change behavior?
faq.answer: Feedback is vague like saying 'be more strategic.' It is delayed weeks after the event. It attacks character instead of describing behavior. It is delivered without trust. It comes as a surprise during annual reviews instead of ongoing conversations. All of these trigger defensiveness.

faq.question: What is the best framework for delivering difficult feedback?
faq.answer: The Situation-Behavior-Impact model works well. Describe the specific situation, the observable behavior you noticed, and the impact it had on others or outcomes. Then ask for the person's perspective. This keeps feedback objective and reduces defensiveness.
